nodes.label: Build and Impact Verification
nodes.rationale: Every pull request explicitly checks build or test status and reviews the affected scope.

nodes.label: Maverick Project Context
nodes.rationale: Maverick is an Unreal Engine 5.6 third-person soulslike, and undocumented structure must be derived from the current codebase.

nodes.label: Policy-First Implementation and Debugging
nodes.rationale: AGENTS.md is a compact entry point; detailed C++ and unity-build rules live in POLICY.md, and runtime tracing precedes a bug-fix decision.

nodes.label: Work and Documentation Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: TODO tracks short-lived task state, while major C++ headers keep compact responsibility and lifecycle contracts adjacent to declarations.

nodes.label: Character and Domain Responsibility Separation
nodes.rationale: CharacterBase types retain shared state, component wiring, and lifecycle bridges; dodge, action buffering, combat, and UI policy remain in domain components.

nodes.label: Graphify Navigation and Freshness Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Existing graph queries narrow investigation; generated artifacts are never hand-edited, incremental updates precede commits, and document-inclusive wrap-up plus freshness verification precedes push.

nodes.label: Trace-First Debugging Policy
nodes.rationale: Filterable runtime traces include frame, actor or component, and key state values so reproduction evidence narrows the cause before implementation.

nodes.label: Unity Build Identifier Safety
nodes.rationale: Because unity builds combine cpp files into one translation unit, local helpers use module-searched domain-specific names and shared logic moves to one explicit utility.

nodes.label: Korean Conventional Commits
nodes.rationale: Conventional Commit categories are retained while titles and bullet-form descriptions use their mapped Korean type names.

nodes.label: Documentation and Graph Governance
nodes.rationale: TODO, canonical wiki documents, adjacent C++ contracts, and Graphify-generated artifacts have distinct ownership and update paths.

nodes.label: Graphify Pre-Push Freshness Gate
nodes.rationale: Changed code and canonical documents must be reflected before commit, and a document-inclusive wrap-up plus deterministic freshness check must pass before push.

nodes.label: Documentation Information Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: TODO owns task state, headers own type-local contracts, docs/wiki owns durable intent, and generated graphs own calculated current relationships.

nodes.label: Graphify Generated Read Models
nodes.rationale: graph.json, generated wiki, Obsidian vault, and GRAPH_REPORT are regenerated views; corrections belong in source code or docs/wiki.

nodes.label: Prompt-Time Query-First Workflow
nodes.rationale: Prompt receipt records context in TODO and queries the existing graph without regeneration, avoiding churn from unaccepted experiments and intermediate state.

nodes.label: Commit-Time Incremental Graphify Update
nodes.rationale: A commit is a coherent snapshot: code-only changes use structural update, document changes require semantic extraction, and the AST-only Git hook remains only a safety net.

nodes.label: Pre-Push Graphify Wrap-Up Gate
nodes.rationale: Knowledge-source changes require TODO review, full code-and-document update, graph health and exports, architecture review when boundaries changed, and a freshness marker before push.

nodes.label: CsvToJsonConverter
nodes.rationale: A dependency-free converter accepts both Client-filtered and plain CSV layouts so design sources can feed one JSON generation path.

nodes.label: UMVTableManager
nodes.rationale: Runtime reads the manifest and generated UDataTable assets rather than the editor-side JSON intermediate.

nodes.label: Maverick Table System
nodes.rationale: The editor pipeline converts CSV through JSON into UDataTable assets, merges directly managed tables into one manifest, and makes those assets the runtime source of truth.

nodes.label: Client Column Filter
nodes.rationale: The Client row preserves editor-only metadata in source CSV while excluding design notes, review state, temporary calculations, and server-only values from runtime tables.

nodes.label: FMVTableRowBase
nodes.rationale: A transient common RowId bridges heterogeneous table key fields into one runtime lookup contract after each typed row copies its own key in PostRead.

nodes.label: Directly Managed DataTables
nodes.rationale: Tables tightly coupled to montages and sections can bypass CSV generation while still participating in the shared runtime manifest.

nodes.label: Table JSON Schema v1
nodes.rationale: The schema is an editor-generation interchange format, not a runtime data source; it carries version, provenance, table keys, and row objects.

nodes.label: SheetRecipe.json
nodes.rationale: This compact table-to-key map lets the DataTable generator associate each table with its key column and row struct without rescanning row payloads.

nodes.label: Typed Row Struct Binding
nodes.rationale: MVTable metadata, matching field names, and PostRead RowId assignment form one binding contract from JSON table identity to typed runtime lookup.

nodes.label: FMVGenericTableRow
nodes.rationale: A generic key-plus-RowJson fallback keeps untyped tables inspectable, while frequently used gameplay tables should graduate to typed row structs.

nodes.label: AI Combat StateTree
nodes.rationale: Combat uses top-down first-true state selection, so narrowly gated attack states precede movement and idle states without starving them.

nodes.label: MVGlobalSensingTask
nodes.rationale: A persistent Combat-parent task centralizes target sensing, path checks, area classification, and cooldown readiness into one continuously refreshed context.

nodes.label: MVCombatDecisionCondition
nodes.rationale: One DesiredState-driven condition keeps state eligibility consistent while attack range remains owned by each candidate rather than CombatMaxDistance.

nodes.label: FMVAICombatActionCandidate
nodes.rationale: Counter, sprint, airborne, skill, and basic attacks share one candidate contract so distance, angle, visibility, path, airborne, and cooldown gates are evaluated uniformly.

nodes.label: Select And Execute Attack Task
nodes.rationale: Multi-candidate states first avoid repeating LastAttackTag, then permit repetition as a fallback so variety does not make an otherwise valid state fail unnecessarily.

nodes.label: Focusing Task
nodes.rationale: Because it remains Running, focusing belongs on a persistent parent or movement state; attack states omit it when montage-time rotation is undesirable.

nodes.label: UMVActionCooldownComponent
nodes.rationale: Global sensing already creates and ticks this cooldown component, so a duplicate Global Action Cooldown Task must not be installed in the same StateTree.

nodes.label: Death Respawn Runtime Flow
nodes.rationale: Each subsystem confirms only the fact it owns and hands the next phase off through events or explicit APIs, separating damage, presentation, UI gating, world reset, and persistence.

nodes.label: UMVHitReactionComponent
nodes.rationale: Lethal knockdown and airborne hits preserve their pre-death reaction until a handoff, while lethal standing hits skip reaction so death presentation starts immediately.

nodes.label: UMVStatComponent
nodes.rationale: The stat component owns lethal-state truth and context publication but deliberately does not choose montages or UI transitions.

nodes.label: UMVDeathComponent
nodes.rationale: This actor-local component chooses and reports death presentation only after lethal state is settled; respawn, loading, and world reset remain outside its responsibility.

nodes.label: UMVActionComponent
nodes.rationale: It stays a policy-free executor of the supplied action row and exposes lifecycle events used by death presentation.

nodes.label: UMVAnimNotify_HitReactionDeathHandoff
nodes.rationale: The notify transfers lethal KD/AB reactions just before Lying, while OnActionEnded remains a fallback when the notify is absent.

nodes.label: UMVDeathRespawnFlow
nodes.rationale: A central gate waits for both death presentation completion and overlay minimum-display completion, preventing montage timing and UI timers from racing.

nodes.label: UMVDeathOverlayWindow
nodes.rationale: The overlay only renders a localized fixed message and reports its timing; it never opens loading or owns game-state transition.

nodes.label: UMVFieldTransitionSubsystem
nodes.rationale: Death respawn and checkpoint travel share loading, reset, relocation, and restoration, so their coordinator uses GameInstance lifetime and delegates actor-specific restoration.

nodes.label: FMVGameGuideRow
nodes.rationale: Reusable guide content is named and modeled by its data meaning rather than one display surface, while domain-owned item lore remains outside this table.

nodes.label: UMVWorldStateSubsystem
nodes.rationale: Persistent facts live in a GameInstance subsystem so checkpoints, consumed spawns, world flags, and quest progress survive map and loading transitions.

nodes.label: UMVQuestSubsystem
nodes.rationale: Quest rules request persistence through WorldState instead of mutating SaveGame directly.

nodes.label: MVFieldTransitionResettableInterface
nodes.rationale: Reset policy and actor restoration stay with each actor domain, avoiding a separate FieldStateSubsystem that would centralize heterogeneous behavior.

nodes.label: Death Input Gate
nodes.rationale: Dead state blocks movement and actions while preserving look input, with each concrete input entry point enforcing the shared state.

nodes.label: MDA: A Formal Approach to Game Design and Game Research
nodes.norm_label: mda: a formal approach to game design and game research

nodes.label: Current Combat Architecture
nodes.rationale: The current project behaves primarily as a close-combat sandbox whose dominant strategy is inexpensive light-attack suppression because long-term progression and several combat contracts are incomplete.

nodes.label: Combat Contract Inconsistency
nodes.rationale: Damage, hit reaction, interruption, invulnerability, launch, movement locking, and hit confirmation currently use inconsistent rules, weakening fairness and outcome trust.

nodes.label: Target Combat Architecture v0.2
nodes.rationale: The target separates simple neutral attacks, role-based skills, weapon grammar, phased armor, and unified hit resolution so rules create readable choices and fair, weighty combat.

nodes.label: Basic Attack Grammar
nodes.rationale: Removing the middle heavy-attack category clarifies the neutral choice as safe light pressure versus committed charge payoff while contextual dodge and sprint attacks remain variations of those categories.

nodes.label: Three Plus One Skill Architecture
nodes.rationale: Three frequent Tempo, Break, and Response slots plus one combat-earned Signature slot preserve learnable roles while enabling tactical expression.

nodes.label: Sidegrade Loadout
nodes.rationale: Alternatives within a slot should solve the same combat problem through different distance, safety, conditions, and failure costs rather than becoming vertical upgrades.

nodes.label: Weapon Combat Grammar
nodes.rationale: Weapons share light and charge categories but must change range, tempo, area control, Impact, commitment, and resource generation rather than only damage values.

nodes.label: Impact Armor Outcome Contract
nodes.rationale: Attack Impact determines whether the current action is interrupted, Armor defines the minimum required Impact, and reaction or movement outcomes remain separate decisions.

nodes.label: Action Phase Armor Profile
nodes.rationale: Armor is computed once from an ArmorProfile and the current Startup, Active, or Recovery phase; montage notifies only announce phase timing to prevent duplicated truth and drift.

nodes.label: Post Reaction Control Resistance
nodes.rationale: A short resistance window after accepted reactions blocks repeated I1 control without blocking damage, groggy buildup, stronger Impact, or death, guaranteeing minimum action opportunity.

nodes.label: ResolvedHitTransaction
nodes.rationale: One resolved transaction records defender outcomes, attacker consequences, execution identity, and hit-confirm tags so damage, cancellation, reaction, launch, feedback, and skill progression share one event.

nodes.label: Damage Immunity
nodes.rationale: Dodge invulnerability should block HP damage, groggy damage, ordinary reaction, and ordinary hit confirmation rather than merely suppressing animation.

nodes.label: Movement Result Policy
nodes.rationale: Hit resolution applies one movement result and source-owned lock token so visual reaction and player control agree and exceptional exits cannot leave stale locks.

nodes.label: Automatic Groggy
nodes.rationale: Groggy triggers immediately on the hit that reaches the threshold so the gauge does not depend on a hidden reaction-type condition.

nodes.label: Attack Documentation Contract
nodes.rationale: Every attack should align role, input, phases, armor, cancellation, cost, hit confirmation, outcomes, feedback, and intended MDA across DataTable, montage, Blueprint, and C++.

nodes.label: Combat Implementation Roadmap
nodes.rationale: Trace existing cancellation paths first, establish the hit transaction and a minimal Impact by Armor vertical slice, then revise movement and basic attacks before validating skills and additional weapons.

nodes.label: Documentation Drift
nodes.rationale: Existing HUD stamina, death-respawn, and AI StateTree documents contain statements older than the inspected implementation or assets and require reconciliation.
